newsitem.title: USA: NFL-PACKERS CRUSH EAGLES AT LAMBEAU FIELD.
newsitem.headline: NFL-PACKERS CRUSH EAGLES AT LAMBEAU FIELD.

text.p: The Green Bay Packers did nothing to discourage backers who pick them for the Super Bowl this season when they crushed the Philadelphia Eagles 39-13 in the first Monday night game at Lambeau Field in 10 years.
Brett Favre threw for 261 yards and three touchdowns -- including two to Robert Brooks -- and the defence intercepted three passes for the Packers.

"This is a great win for us," said Packers coach Mike Holmgren. "We know we have a good football team. How far we can go, I don't know. If we can stay away from injuries and stay focused, we can have a very good season."

Favre, who completed 17-of-31 passes, found Brooks on scoring passes of 25 and 20 yards in the first half. Brooks finished with five receptions for 130 yards, the 10th 100-yard effort of his career. Running back Edgar Bennett had 17 carries for 93 yards and five receptions for 49 yards.

The Packers (2-0) reaped all four Philadelphia turnovers -- three interceptions and a fumble -- in the first half en route to a 30-7 halftime lead. But the defence did collect a safety for Green Bay in the second half.
"We forced 10 turnovers in our first two games," said Holmgren. "We forced only 16 in all of last year. Forcing turnovers can be contagious."

"If we as a defence can put our offence in the position to score, we are going to be very successful," said defensive star Reggie White. "We want to force a lot of turnovers. That is what we did tonight."
Favre, the 1995 Most Valuable Player who spent part of the off-season in a rehabilitation centre recovering from an addiction to painkillers, has seven touchdowns through two games thus far.

"We were worried whether our wide receivers could beat their bump-and-run defence," Favre said. "You saw what happened tonight. Robert Brooks versus any bump-and-run defence is a great matchup for us."
Chris Jacke added three first-half field goals as the Packers emerged as the NFL's highest scoring team through two weeks. The Packers are a league-best 15-2 at home over the last two seasons.
The game, which set an attendance record at Lambeau Field, was the first Monday night game at the legendary stadium since Sept. 22, 1986.
Philadelphia (1-1) was held to just 59 yards on the ground and gave up its most points since surrendering 48 to the Oakland Raiders in Week 4 of last season.
The Eagles, who were seeking to start the season 2-0 for the first time since 1992, managed just two short touchdown runs in the second and fourth quarters.
"We were physically dominated on both sides of the ball," said Eagles coach Ray Rhodes. "The turnovers killed us."
Rhodes added: "I thought we were a little better than we are. When you come up against a team like them, you really see where you are."

Early in the first quarter, cornerback Doug Evans recovered Eagles wide receiver Chris Jones's fumble at the Philadelphia 14. Green Bay, which started slowly, settled for a 29-yard field goal from Jacke.

Favre's first touchdown pass to Brooks, with 1:40 left in the opening quarter, made it 10-0 and capped a five-play, 57-yard drive featuring an 11-yard pass to Bennett and a 20-yard strike to tight end Mark Chmura.
After an interception by linebacker George Koonce ended the Eagles' next possession, Jacke converted a 44-yard attempt four seconds into the second quarter to make it 13-0.
The Packers made it 20-0 on their next drive when Bennett ripped off runs of 16 and 11 yards, setting up a one-yard plunge by Dorsey Levens.
Green Bay got the ball back again and converted it into a 23-0 advantage. Favre found Brooks with a 33-yard completion to the Eagles 40 just prior to Jacke's 38-yard field goal.

The Eagles finally got on the board. After Eagles quarterback Rodney Peete hit Jones for a 33-yard pass the Philadelphia wide receiver lateralled the ball to Irving Fryar, who took it to the Packers 1. Rickey Watters then scored on a one-yard run to cut the deficit to 23-7.
Peete was 10-of-25 for 142 yards but was picked off three times while Watters finished with 10 carries for 38 yards.
Favre then executed the two-minute offence to perfection, finding Keith Jackson for an 18-yard pass on 3rd-and-9, completing a 21-yard toss to Antonio Freeman and hitting Brooks for a 20-yard score.

Bennett caught a 25-yard touchdown pass from Favre on Green Bay's first possession of the second half and White and Santana Dotson shared a sack of Peete in the end zone for a safety before Charlie Garner's touchdown for Philadelphia capped the scoring.
